purpose: When each 2005-06 end-of-season award was announced, who voted and how ballots were scored, researched October 2026. Dates and rules only: no real 2006 winner or vote is recorded or used.

status_values.derived: inferred from cited sources, reasoning given
status_values.design_choice: not verifiable for 2005-06; the simulation's documented choice

ballot_due.note: After the last regular-season games (2006-04-19) and before the first media award (2006-04-25); no source states the deadline.

awards.name: Coach of the Year
awards.note: Announced Tuesday, April 25, 2006 (AP text: 'honored as the NBA's coach of the year Tuesday'; read in a same-day forum repost, so a secondary copy). Scoring 5-3-1 as for the other media awards (derived). Electorate: the Basketball-Reference first-place votes sum to 124, which this file uses; its stated maximum is 630 (126 x 5), so the panel size is not settled by the sources read.

awards.name: Sixth Man of the Year
awards.note: Announced Friday, April 28, 2006 (AP via Deseret News, April 29: 'won the NBA's Sixth Man Award Friday'). Electorate: Basketball-Reference first-place votes sum to 123 and its maximum is 615 (123 x 5). Scoring 5-3-1 (derived).

awards.name: Most Improved Player
awards.note: Announced Monday, May 1, 2006 (AP via CBC, published May 1, 9:34 p.m. EDT: 'of a possible 124 first-place votes'). Basketball-Reference shows first-place votes summing to 126 and a maximum of 630; the 124 stated in the contemporaneous report is used. Scoring 5-3-1 (derived).

awards.name: All-Rookie Teams
awards.voters: head coaches, not for their own players
awards.note: AP via KSL, May 4, 2006: named 'on Thursday' in 'balloting by the league's head coaches'. A unanimous player received 58 points (29 x 2), the Basketball-Reference maximum, so coaches did not vote for their own players (derived). Scoring 2-1 as in 2004-05 (derived).

awards.name: Most Valuable Player
awards.note: Announced Sunday, May 7, 2006 (Honolulu Advertiser, May 8: 'results announced yesterday'; 'a panel of 125 sports writers and broadcasters in the United States and Canada'). Basketball-Reference maximum 1250 (125 x 10). Scoring 10-7-5-3-1 as in 2004-05 (derived).

awards.name: Defensive Player of the Year
awards.note: NBA club release published Monday, May 8, 2006; AP via ESPN: 'of 124 first-place votes'. Basketball-Reference maximum 620 (124 x 5). An AP report of May 7 cited a team source before the announcement; the official date is used. Scoring 5-3-1 (derived).

awards.name: Rookie of the Year
awards.note: NBA club release published Wednesday, May 10, 2006; AP via KSL the same day: 'the 125 first-place votes from a panel of media members'. Basketball-Reference maximum 625 (125 x 5). Scoring 5-3-1 (derived).

awards.name: All-Defensive Teams
awards.voters: head coaches, not for their own players
awards.note: SportsTicker via ESPN, May 11, 2006: named 'on Thursday' in 'voting among the league's 30 coaches'. Two points for a first-team vote, one for a second-team vote, by position, and own-player exclusion as in 2004-05 (derived). Basketball-Reference gives a maximum of 60.

awards.name: All-NBA Teams
awards.note: NBA club release published May 17, 2006: 'The 126-member voting panel ... voted for All-NBA First, Second and Third Teams by position with points awarded on a 5-3-1 basis.' Basketball-Reference maximum 630 (126 x 5).

awards.name: Finals MVP
awards.note: Announced on court the night the Finals are clinched (sourced). Each panelist names one player (sourced). The 2006 ballot count is not published (bballhistorydatabase lists it as N/A); ten ballots were counted in 2005 and 2007, so the electorate of 10 is carried from 2004-05 (design choice). An even panel can split: a tie at the top is an engine decision draw (no published tie rule; the award has never been shared). A player on the losing club may win (Jerry West, 1969).

not_decided.name: Sportsmanship Award
not_decided.reason: a player-ballot character award with no evidence basis in simulated results; no sourced 2006 date
